title: Offline optimizer guardrails for Private/VPC: hardened policy enforcement and rollback-proof apply
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement hardened guardrails for Redwood's optimization automation (batching/caching recommendations and automated config applies) that are safe to run in Private/VPC/on-prem environments. This ticket covers: (1) offline validation of suggested config changes without egress, (2) a cryptographically verifiable apply protocol for air-gapped agents, (3) policy enforcement surface (admission checks and operator-configured deny-lists), and (4) rollback-proof versioning + canary rollback workflows usable in restricted networks.
background: Customers in regulated environments require optimizer suggestions but cannot allow a cloud control plane to push live changes, or to leak telemetry. Prior work implemented autosuggesters for hosted environments; Private clusters currently receive raw suggestions but the apply step is manual and error-prone. Several incidents highlighted misapplied batching profiles causing latency spikes in production when KV caches were incompatible with quantized kernels. We need an offline-first, policy-driven flow that operators can audit and run without exposing sensitive telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Offline validation harness that can run locally in air-gapped clusters and produce a deterministic diff report for proposed batching/caching changes
Apply protocol that requires signed manifests (private key held by customer) and includes a dry-run mode that simulates latency/cost impacts using locally sampled traces
Admission/time-of-apply policy engine (OPA/rego or Kubernetes admission) that enforces operator-configured constraints such as max_batch_size, max_latency_increase_pct, and disabled_automations
Automatic rollback mechanism that uses immutable config versions with safe rollback hooks and a canary grouping facility; rollback must not require outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane
Telemetry and audit log mode that redacts PII and can be configured to keep counters locally only (no external upload) or to export summaries under customer consent
E2E tests covering an air-gapped agent applying, rejecting, and rolling back a suggested change using local KMS/HSM sign/verify flow
tasks: Spec: offline validation binary + diff format (JSON + HTML) — define inputs/outputs and simulated workload profile format
Spec: signed manifest format and key management integration (KMS/HSM offline signing + verification)
Implement: offline validation harness prototype (go binary) that consumes token/trace samples and runs cost/latency model locally
Implement: agent-side apply flow that verifies signature, enforces admission policies, stages changes to immutable versioned store, and optionally performs canary rollout
Implement: admission policy library with default safe rules for Private (deny auto-enable of batching if KV cache not present, require explicit opt-in for aggressive quantization suggestions)
Integrate: local telemetry redaction + option to write audit bundle to mounted storage for operator retrieval
Add: CI job that runs air-gap e2e simulation using containerized agent and offline harness
Docs: operator runbook for manual approve/dry-run/apply/rollback in air-gapped clusters
Security review: threat model update and KMS/HSM secret handling checklist
notes: Decision: prefer OPA style policies evaluated at the agent to avoid added network hops. Policy language must be expressive enough for numerical thresholds and allowlisting specific models.

Trade-off: fully automatic applies are disallowed by default in Private mode; heavy emphasis on dry-run + operator approval. We will provide a reversible canary that can be scripted but never forced without operator consent.
Performance model: the offline validator will use aggregated token-latency histograms and a light-weight analytical model rather than full re-run to avoid heavy compute in on-prem clusters.
Privacy: sample traces used for simulation must be scrubbed; we will provide tooling to remove prompt text and replace with token-length distributions before any export.
KMS: support both cloud KMS connectors (with offline signing via importable key material) and customer HSM where available. Verification uses public key bundles stored in agent config.
Fallbacks: if KV cache metadata is missing, the admission policy will mark batching recommendations as blocked and suggest a safe default (single-request mode) until metadata collected.

Rollbacks: store previous config versions immutable and provide a local fast-path to revert to previous version within a configurable window (default 15 minutes). For longer windows, operator must escalate via documented procedure.
